botAccessAudit.method: curl with 15 first-party-documented bot UA strings (see geo/01-bot-uas.txt) plus a curl-default and a real-Chrome-UA control, against 5 routes: /, /listings/hampton-inn-shelbyville, /insights/hotel-refinancing-wave-2026, /team, /contact.
botAccessAudit.result: PASS, clean. All 17 UA variants returned identical HTTP 200, identical byte length, and identical sha256 body hash on every one of the 5 routes tested. No 403/429/401, no JS/WAF challenge page, no x-robots-tag header anywhere, no cloaking. No UA-based differentiation of any kind observed.
botAccessAudit.caveat: ClaudeBot/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot exact UA strings are NOT published verbatim by Anthropic's own support article (it names the robots.txt tokens but gives no literal UA string); the string tested is the most common third-party-reported form. This does not change the PASS result (the server doesn't appear to branch on UA at all) but flagging per the 'no source, say so' rule.

structuredData.sharedGraphNote: CORRECTION to the mission-brief's characterization ('no shared entity source and no @graph'): src/app/layout.tsx DOES define a shared @graph with @id-addressable nodes (`${SITE_URL}/#org` as RealEstateAgent, `${SITE_URL}/#website`), and most route files (closed/[slug], glossary/[term], insights/[slug], markets/[city], services/[slug], research/mhi/[quarter], listings/[slug], hotels-for-sale/[brand], offices/[slug], team/[slug]) reference it correctly via {"@id": "${SITE_URL}/#org"}. What IS true and worth fixing: this shared node is a hardcoded literal object inside layout.tsx, not an imported constant from a single lib/entity.ts module, so every reference is a bare string match on the URL rather than a typed import -- fragile to rename, and not actually 'DRY' at the source-code level even though the runtime graph is correctly connected. team/[slug] additionally emits a redundant inline `parentOrganization` Organization node (name only, no @id) alongside its correct `worksFor`/`affiliation` @id references -- harmless duplication, not a contradiction.

competitorBaseline.summary: Of the 20 seed prompts, matthewshotelmarkets.com appeared in results for only 8 (all brand-anchored: contains 'Matthews'). For all 12 generic/category prompts (e.g. 'Who are the best hotel brokers in Texas?', 'Hotel brokers in Austin, Texas', 'Top hotel investment sales brokerages in the US in 2026', 'Who sells boutique hotels in the Texas Hill Country?'), matthewshotelmarkets.com did not appear at all -- named competitors instead: CBRE Hotels, Marcus & Millichap, JLL Hotels & Hospitality Group, Colliers Hotels, HotelAVE, Hunter (Hotel) Advisors, HREC, Eastdil Secured, Berkadia, US Hotel Advisors, HTL Hospitality Advisors, Tabani Realty, Singh Commercial Group, Hotel Brokers of America/International/Austin, F10 Hotels, Bridge Marketplace, CMBS.Loans, The Plasencia Group, HotelBrokerOne. Even for the 8 brand-anchored prompts, www.matthews.com (the parent) outranked matthewshotelmarkets.com in most of them, and AI-style summaries pulled specific facts (deal names, figures) almost entirely from matthews.com press releases/success stories, not from matthewshotelmarkets.com's own /closed or /team pages.
